assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data has changed how economists measure opportunity, neighbourhood effects and mobility. The work is also credible by design: very large samples, quasi-experimental designs and transparent data. It has shaped both academic research and policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the central figure, with Hendren and Friedman as the closest collaborators on mobility and neighbourhood effects. Lawrence Katz is a significant contributor but is left out to respect the three-person limit. Chetty's wider body of work, including tax and teacher value-added studies, could blur which discovery the prize would name.
assessment.maturity: The core results date from roughly 2014 to 2022. There has been time for replication and extension, and for debate over identification and the causal reading of place effects. Policy impact is still unfolding, but the evidence base is substantial.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to recognise Chetty for a broader portfolio than this single topic
Contested causal interpretation of some place-based and mobility estimates
Relative youth of the laureate group compared with long-waiting candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The China-shock studies and the task-based account of technology reshaped how economists think about trade, automation, local labour markets and inequality. The work is empirically transparent and has had large influence on policy and public debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure across both technology and trade. Hanson and Dorn are the co-authors on the trade-shock papers. The task framework overlaps with the work of Acemoglu, who was recognised in 2024, and with earlier work by Katz, Levy and Murnane, which complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: The core papers appeared between 2003 and 2016 and have been widely replicated and extended. Some conclusions about durability and mechanisms have been refined or qualified. The research programme is mature but still active.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior recognition of technology and institutions work
Sensitivity of shift-share designs to identification critiques
Whether Lawrence Katz should be included instead of Dorn

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Methods for heterogeneous treatment effects, causal forests and double/debiased machine learning give applied economists a credible framework for using flexible prediction in causal analysis. The framework is widely adopted and improves the credibility of empirical work.
assessment.attribution: Athey, Wager and Chernozhukov all have clear, distinct roles. Chernozhukov's contribution also appears in the quantile regression candidacy, and Athey's in the IT and digital markets candidacy. Fellow contributors such as Imbens, Newey and Hansen are either already recognised or sit in other groups. The credit assignment is contestable.
assessment.maturity: The main papers date from about 2016 to 2018. Adoption is rapid, but the long-run durability of specific estimators is not yet settled. Wager is a relatively junior name.
uncertainties: Recency, and whether the methods will remain central as machine learning evolves
Ambiguity about how credit is divided with other contributors in this area
Possible preference for a more established methodological topic

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Management practices as a measurable driver of firm productivity, supported by field experiments and large-scale surveys, explain a good share of productivity dispersion across firms and countries. The work links organisational economics to growth and has policy relevance. Randomised evidence in firms adds credibility.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are the clear leads. Sadun is a significant co-author but a more junior contributor to the core programme. Bloom is also named on the uncertainty-shocks candidacy, which could dilute or split credit.
assessment.maturity: The work spans about 2007 to 2020 with experiments in India and extended survey data. It is reasonably mature. Questions remain about measurement validity and generalisability of the management score.
uncertainties: Measurement validity of survey-based management scores
External validity of the experimental evidence
Overlap with other candidacies involving Bloom

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Combines theory and credible empirical measurement of adverse selection and moral hazard in insurance markets. It includes experimental and quasi-experimental evidence such as the Oregon health insurance experiment. It has influenced health policy design and the empirical practice of contract theory. The methodological bar is high.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav are the strongest empirical drivers. Salanie's contribution is more theoretical and methodological, so the three-person grouping is somewhat loose. Many other researchers contributed to the broader health insurance literature.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 2005 to the present and the evidence base is well developed. It is relatively recent for Nobel recognition, but no major robustness concern has overturned it.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as one coherent discovery or several contributions
Weighting of theory relative to empirics in the credit
Possible preference for more senior names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of fairness and reciprocity, together with the experimental evidence on strong reciprocity and costly punishment, made social preferences a central part of economic modelling. The work has influenced contract theory, public goods and labour economics. Its replicability is stronger than that of some behavioural findings, though it is debated.
assessment.attribution: The Fehr-Schmidt 1999 model and the related Bolton-Ockenfels framework were developed in parallel, and Bolton is not on this list. Falk has made large contributions on measuring preferences. The two-person selection reflects the clearest theory-and-experiment pairing, but credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: The core work dates from about 1993 to 2005. It is very mature, with extensive replication and field validation. Behavioural economics has already been recognised in 2002, 2013, 2017 and 2019, which may reduce the field's marginal priority.
uncertainties: Parallel development by Bolton and Ockenfels, who are not on the list
Questions about the stability of preference estimates and external validity beyond the lab
Prior recognition of behavioural topics

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Systematic formal and empirical analysis of how constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity shape fiscal and policy outcomes has defined modern political economics. The work spans theory and empirics and has influenced both economics and political science.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the closest pairing through their joint work on political economics, with Besley's contributions on state capacity, accountability and political agency. The Acemoglu-Johnson-Robinson prize in 2024 covers neighbouring ground on institutions, which complicates distinctiveness.
assessment.maturity: The work is very mature, dating from the 1990s and 2000s, and well absorbed into the field. Some empirical results on the effects of electoral rules face identification questions.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 recognition of institutions and prosperity
Causal identification in cross-country constitutional comparisons
Possible institutional proximity to the committee, disclosed but not adjudicated

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model gave a tractable, non-cooperative foundation for bargaining and underpins work in labour, markets and political economy. It is a classic theoretical contribution with lasting influence.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein's 1982 model is the key result. Related work by Ståhl, and the market-bargaining extensions by Wolinsky and Binmore, are significant but secondary. Naming Rubinstein alone gives the cleanest attribution but may understate the collaborative extension work.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with over four decades of use. The main risk is that the prize timing may seem late or that game theory has received considerable recent recognition.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would add Wolinsky or Binmore
Competition from other game-theory and mechanism-design-related topics
Limited direct empirical testability of the model
